# WO-2026-08-11-B15-COCKPIT-BE-01 — Cockpit backend: canonical state, command-surface wiring, Telegram shapes

## Acceptance criteria

AC1: One canonical six-value state (`NEEDS_WARWICK` / `ASDAIR_WORKING` / `READY_FOR_WARWICK` / `BROWSER_WORKING` / `COMPLETE` / `FAILED`) is exposed via exactly one `services/asdair/cockpit-api/**` function/endpoint, computed by reading a value rather than being independently recomputed from raw counts in cockpit-api or `services/cockpit/**`. Checkable by: grep for any second, independent state-derivation logic outside that one function.
AC2: Every write action reachable through `services/asdair/cockpit-api/commandSurface.js` (answering a question, correcting a line, marking "not this week") calls into the existing `answer()` / `correctLine` pipeline functions — no new direct database write bypassing them. Checkable by: reading every new/changed exported function in commandSurface.js and tracing its write path.
AC3: `shopLines.markCorrected` has at least one real, exercised production caller newly reachable from the Cockpit write path (per `acceptance_property` above) — or is explicitly, visibly superseded by a differently-named equivalent, stated as such in the final report, never silently.
AC4: `services/asdair/bot/renderMessages.js` and `sendShopperMessage.js` implement exactly three notification message shapes (list read / shop ready / basket built) and no longer send a per-question card per open decision.
AC5: All touched-package tests pass with a non-zero executed count reported (`node --test` or the project's existing convention per sibling files) — a callable script with no execution is not evidence.

- The exact test-runner invocation used for touched packages, with its reported pass count (non-zero) pasted into the final report — not just "tests pass."
